question_stem:
A double-slit interference experiment is set up using monochromatic light of wavelength $580\text{ nm}$, as shown in Fig. 4.1.

{{figure:figure_4_1}}

Fig. 4.1

The slit separation is $a = 0.41\text{ mm}$. A screen is placed parallel to the slits at distance $D$. A bright fringe is observed at central point X, and adjacent dark fringes are observed at Y and Z. The distance between Y and Z is $4.0\text{ mm}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State what is meant by the diffraction of a wave.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Explain why a bright fringe is produced at point X.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: State the difference in the distances, in nm, from each slit to point Y.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text:
The intensity of the light passing through the two slits was initially the same. The intensity of the light through one of the slits is now reduced.

Compare the appearance of the fringes before and after the change of intensity.
